athlete.bio: A tenacious L/DS with an unwavering spirit, this Kansas player embodies resilience and tactical acumen, weaving through opponents with agility and sharp instincts, always ready to uplift teammates on and off the court.

caption:
If only everyone could be lucky enough to find a program as perfect for them as Kansas Volleyball was for me. Perfect, not because it was easy or all sunshine and rainbows, but because of a coaching staff full of love and teaching, a community full of support and cheer, roommates who make you laugh till you cry, and experiences that allow you to grow as a human and a player. College volleyball is all about showing you your greatest offering is not always something you do, but most often it’s the person you become in the process. 

Kansas volleyball is one of those places that every young volleyball player dreams of being a part of and i’ve been the luckiest girl in the world to be able to experience it, even if it was only for 8 months. Never in my life did this freshman walk on believe she would make it to captain a sweet sixteen team in her final year, but boy would she be so giddy to see me now. Not only to see that, but to know how many people supported her in those efforts, from both osu and ku communities, and the growth she underwent to get there. Thank you Kansas Volleyball for all you’ve done to keep my volleyball flame burning bright, I love you forever #22💙

caption:
Thank you travel ball. 
-
After over 10 years of playing, it’s hard to put into words just how much travel softball has meant to me. I didn’t have the typical summers most kids do—mine were spent at the fields, in cages, and on the road. But looking back, I wouldn’t change a thing. I’m so incredibly grateful for the opportunities this sport has blessed me with. The friendships, the memories, the lessons learned—all of it made the long days and tough losses more than worth it. Travel softball gave me a second family and showed me what it means to have grit, determination, and passion. This community shaped me into the player and person I am today, and I’ll carry everything it’s taught me into this next chapter. It’s a bittersweet goodbye, but I’m filled with excitement for what lies ahead.
Thank you, travel softball. You’ll always have a piece of my heart.

I think about the day I sat in my living room with my brothers, watching NCAA college basketball and told myself, “ I’ll be there one day” I just didn’t know when.

I want to thank Coach Bill Self, and the rest of the Kansas Jayhawks coaching staff for this amazing opportunity. A huge thank you as well to everyone who played a pivotal role in making this happen— my family, friends and @athletesinpower team.

caption: Words can’t express how grateful I am for these last two weeks. The people I met and grew close to were so amazing and I am forever thankful for them. Something I learned in these past weeks is that everyone is introduced into our lives for a reason. A lot of the time, we are blessed with great people like I was these past weeks. However, sometimes people are placed into our lives that can be challenging to deal with. We are often very passive with these people the same way we can be with our faith - lacking intentionality because we think we have plenty of time. Ephesians 5:15-16 says, “Look carefully then how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, making the best use of the time, because the days are evil.” We never know how much time we have, nor do we know how much time the people around us do. As Christians, we need to be intentional with our time. Not only so we can grow in our own relationships with God, but so that we can introduce him to others around us. We are called to be fishers of men, loving and uplifting the people around us in all that we do. I am forever grateful for the lessons I have learned at this place. Thank you Kanakuk for the best 11 years - you will always have a special place in my heart. @kanakukkseven #kanakuk

caption: To know this team is to love this team! None of us could have done any of this without each and everyone of these girls on this team. Thank you Washington softball for giving me these girls that I can call FAMILY! Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to make some of the most special memories with these girls, I wouldn’t trade it for the world! I want to thank all my friends and family who have came and watched me and supported me throughout this season. It meant more than you will ever know. When I got hurt during slow pitch last year I thought I wasn’t going to be able to play with this team one last time and the thought made me sick to my stomach. God allowed me to play through the pain so that I was able to play my senior year of fast pitch for my family. The coaches in this program have a special place in my heart and have pushed me hard but loved me even harder and for that I thank them. This year was special not only because of winning state for the third time in a row but because this team went through a lot of ups and downs throughout the season. We went through a lot but we always had each other to look back on to be a shoulder to cry on, a person to vent to, or even a person to make us laugh and have a great time. I could go on and on about this team but I will end it here. caption:
Dear Mom,

I have a lot of things I wish i could have said to you while you were still here.  This has been the most difficult thing i have had to deal with in awhile.  It has taken me some time to collect my thoughts and emotions into something. Everyday I wish things could have been different. I wish i could have been there for you at the end. I wish i could have given you the comfort that you always searched so desperately for. I wish i could have told you how much i love you, how much all of your kids love you and I hope you knew that. It’s a hard thing for Eli and Naomi to understand but for us it has always been different. When we were together I admired every second i was with you.  We had some good times mom but unfortunately life took us on two separate routes.  I can only imagine how hard the adoption was on you. But i am forever grateful for your courage and the strength that it took to give your kids up.  That’s a sacrifice that no parent should ever have to make but you did it because you loved us. Without that decision who knows where we would be today.  Losing you once was hard. At a young age it didn’t really occur to me that i probably wouldn’t get to see you again. I prayed for your health i prayed that you would get better i prayed that someday things may be good again. It makes me beyond happy to hear that you were doing well. Death is inevitable though. No one knows when it is going to come and how it might affect you. Getting that news broke me. It’s not fair that i had to lose you twice. It’s not fair that we didn’t get our happily ever after. But as i sit back and reflect my perspective changes. God works in very mysterious ways and all we can do is have faith in his plan. You found your faith again, you gave your life back to God. That is the ultimate happily ever after. Selfishly i wish you didn’t have to go but God had different plans for you. He called your beautiful soul home. No more pain no more suffering. I am so happy to know that you are home and you are released from this world. You had chains on in this world that were weighing you down. Now you can finally fly and be free. I will always miss you and I will FOREVER love you .
